items.title: Practical-Approach-Difference: Four Combinations of Painful, Pleasant, Slow, and Fast

items.zh: 云何由行迹差別建立補特伽羅？謂如所舉、如所開示補特伽羅，依四行迹而得出離。何等為四？謂或有行迹是苦遲通，或有行迹是苦速通，或有行迹是樂遲通，或有行迹是樂速通。當知此中，若鈍根性補特伽羅，未得根本靜慮，所有行迹，名苦遲通。若利根性補特伽羅，未得根本靜慮，所有行迹，名苦速通。若鈍根性補特伽羅，已得根本靜慮，所有行迹，名樂遲通。
items.en: How does difference of practical approach classify practitioners? The practitioners already named and explained reach liberation by one of four practical approaches. What are the four? The painful-and-slow path, the painful-and-fast path, the pleasant-and-slow path, and the pleasant-and-fast path. Know that a dull-facultied practitioner who has not attained the root absorption follows the painful-and-slow path. A sharp-facultied practitioner who has not attained the root absorption follows the painful-and-fast path. A dull-facultied practitioner who has attained the root absorption follows the pleasant-and-slow path.

items.title: Section: Six Remaining Principles Close Establishing Practitioners in Full

items.zh: 若利根性補特伽羅，已得根本靜慮，所有行迹，名樂速通。如是名為由行迹差別建立補特伽羅。云何由道果差別建立補特伽羅？謂行四向及住四果。行四向者，一、預流果向補特伽羅，二、一來果向補特伽羅，三、不還果向補特伽羅，四、阿羅漢果向補特伽羅。住四果者，一、預流果，二、一來果，三、不還果，四、阿羅漢果。若於向道轉，彼名行向者。由向道故，建立四種補特伽羅。若得沙門果，彼名住果者。由道果故，建立四種補特伽羅。如是名為由道果差別建立補特伽羅。云何由加行差別建立補特伽羅？謂隨信行及隨法行補特伽羅。若隨補特伽羅信，勤修正行，名隨信行補特伽羅。若於諸法不待他緣，隨毘柰耶勤修正行，名隨法行補特伽羅。如是名為由加行差別建立補特伽羅。云何由定差別建立補特伽羅？謂身證補特伽羅，於八解脫身已作證具足安住，而未獲得諸漏永盡。當知如是補特伽羅，於有色觀諸色解脫、內無色想觀外諸色解脫、淨解脫身作證具足住、空無邊處解脫、識無邊處解脫、無所有處解脫、非想非非想處解脫、想受滅解脫，已能順逆入出自在。如是名為由定差別建立補特伽羅。云何由生差別建立補特伽羅？謂極七返有、家家、一間、中般涅槃、生般涅槃、無行般涅槃、有行般涅槃、及以上流補特伽羅。如是名為由生差別建立補特伽羅。云何由退不退差別建立補特伽羅？謂由退故，建立時解脫阿羅漢，彼於現法樂住容有退失。由不退故，建立不動法阿羅漢，彼於現法樂住定無退失。如是名為由退不退差別建立補特伽羅。云何由障差別建立補特伽羅？謂慧解脫及俱分解脫阿羅漢。慧解脫阿羅漢者，謂已解脫煩惱障，未解脫定障。俱分解脫阿羅漢者，謂已解脫煩惱障及已解脫定障，是故說名俱分解脫。
items.en: A sharp-facultied practitioner who has attained the root absorption follows the pleasant-and-fast path. [Path-fruit-difference:] this establishes those approaching each of the four fruits and those abiding in each of the four fruits. [Effort-difference:] this establishes faith-followers and dharma-followers. [Concentration-difference:] this establishes the body-witness, who has fully realised the eight liberations through direct experience yet has not yet permanently exhausted every outflow. [Rebirth-difference:] this establishes those bound for at most seven rebirths, family-to-family practitioners, those with one interval remaining, and the seven destinies culminating in nirvana. [Retrogression-difference:] through susceptibility to retrogression, the time-liberated arhat is established; through its absence, the unshakeable arhat is established. [Obstruction-difference:] this establishes the wisdom-liberated arhat, who has overcome the obstruction of affliction but not the obstruction of concentration, and the both-liberated arhat, who has overcome both.

items.zh: 如是名為由障差別建立補特伽羅。

items.title: Section: Establishing Practitioners Closes; The Object of Meditation Opens

items.zh: 由此所舉及所開示差別道理，如其次第，應知建立補特伽羅。云何所緣？謂有四種所緣境事。何等為四？一者、遍滿所緣境事，二者、淨行所緣境事，三者、善巧所緣境事，四者、淨惑所緣境事。云何遍滿所緣境事？謂復四種。一、有分別影像，二、無分別影像，三、事邊際性，四、所作成辦。
items.en: By the practitioners already named, and by the distinct principles explained, in their proper order, the classification of practitioners should be understood. What is the object of meditation? There are four kinds of object. What are the four? Pervasive objects, purifying objects, skilful objects, and objects that purify affliction. What are pervasive objects? There are, moreover, four: the image accompanied by discrimination, the image free of discrimination, the very limit of things, and the task accomplished.

blocks.text: The classification of practitioners ends with four "practical approaches". Then begins one of the most important topics in the whole Śrāvaka Stage: the **objects of meditation** (所緣).

Painful and slow; painful and fast; pleasant and slow; pleasant and fast. "A dull-facultied practitioner who has not attained the root absorption follows the painful-and-slow path"; "a sharp-facultied practitioner who has attained the root absorption follows the pleasant-and-fast path."

Path and fruit; practice; attainment; and so on. "Through susceptibility to retrogression, the time-liberated arhat is established." The wisdom-liberated arhat "has overcome the obstruction of affliction but not the obstruction of concentration".

items: **Pervasive objects** (遍滿所緣): present in every meditation.
**Purifying objects** (淨行所緣): for purifying a particular temperament.
**Skilful objects** (善巧所緣): for skill in the aggregates, elements, sense-fields, dependent origination, and what is and is not possible.
**Objects for purifying affliction** (淨惑所緣): for the mundane and supramundane paths.

blocks.text: The pervasive object has four aspects: the image **with discrimination** (insight), the image **without discrimination** (calm), the **limit of things**, and **task accomplished**. Venerable Miào Jìng: the limit of things is reaching the path of seeing.

quiz.q: What are the four practical approaches, and what does Venerable Miào Jìng say determines painful/pleasant and slow/fast?
options: painful-slow, painful-fast, pleasant-slow, pleasant-fast; painful or pleasant depends on having the absorptions, slow or fast on dull or sharp faculties
quiz.why: "The painful-and-slow path, the painful-and-fast path, the pleasant-and-slow path, and the pleasant-and-fast path." Venerable Miào Jìng: painful or pleasant depends on whether one has the four absorptions; slow or fast on whether faculties are dull or sharp.

quiz.q: Are the four approaches better or worse than one another, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: all reach nirvāṇa — no better or worse, just faster or slower, harder or easier along the way
quiz.why: "A dull-facultied practitioner who has not attained the root absorption follows the painful-and-slow path." Master Cháng Bǎi: all reach nirvāṇa; none is better or worse — there are only differences of speed and ease along the way.

quiz.q: The time-liberated arhat is established by susceptibility to retrogression. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say regresses?
options: only present meditative ease; the wisdom of non-self never regresses
quiz.why: "Through susceptibility to retrogression, the time-liberated arhat is established." Venerable Miào Jìng: the wisdom of non-self they attained never regresses; only their present meditative ease regresses — that is what "retrogression" means.

quiz.q: The wisdom-liberated are free of the affliction-obstruction but not the concentration-obstruction. How does Venerable Miào Jìng, following the Kośa, define the two?
options: the affliction-obstruction is defiled ignorance; the concentration-obstruction is undefiled ignorance
quiz.why: "The wisdom-liberated arhat … has overcome the obstruction of affliction but not the obstruction of concentration." Venerable Miào Jìng: the affliction-obstruction is defiled ignorance; the concentration-obstruction is undefiled ignorance.

quiz.q: What are the four kinds of object, and what does Venerable Miào Jìng say this question is about?
options: pervasive, purifying, skilful, and affliction-purifying objects; earlier was about people, now about practice
quiz.why: "Pervasive objects, purifying objects, skilful objects, and objects that purify affliction." Venerable Miào Jìng: the earlier questions on kinds and classification of practitioners concerned people; now "object" concerns practice.

quiz.q: Pervasive objects include images with and without discrimination. What does Master Cháng Bǎi say distinguishes calming from insight?
options: not by object — either truth can serve as the object of calming or insight
quiz.why: "The image accompanied by discrimination, the image free of discrimination, the very limit of things, and the task accomplished." Master Cháng Bǎi: calming and insight are not distinguished by their object; either of the two truths can be the object of calming or of insight.

quiz.q: Do the lectures map the four pervasive objects onto stages of the path?
options: Miào Jìng maps stages — the limit of things is entering the path of seeing; Cháng Bǎi says complete task-accomplishment belongs only to the non-learner
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the limit of things is reaching the path of seeing — entering the noble stage from the inner ordinary stage. Master Cháng Bǎi: only the transcendent purity realised at the non-learner stage is complete task-accomplishment. The note does not map stages.
